paper: Nakazono et al. 2022, PLoS ONE, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0258283 (BVBRC-113)
verdict_context: PARTIAL (74/100) --- sequence-level claims replicate; wet-lab claims not tested

open_questions.q: Is the epidermin biosynthetic gene cluster on pEpi56 (OK031036) truly complete and self-sufficient for lantibiotic maturation, or does KSE56 also carry chromosomal accessory genes (e.g., a second copy of a protease, ABC transporter, or immunity determinant) that are required in trans for full epidermin production?
open_questions.basis: The paper reports the epi cluster (epiABCDEFGHPQTY-like) on pEpi56 and demonstrates plasmid-borne activity, but the in-silico replication only enumerated 11 named epi loci on OK031036 and could not evaluate whether curing pEpi56 fully abolishes activity or whether the chromosome supplies redundant functions. epiY absence in the deposited annotation vs its discussion in the paper's Fig 2B relative to Tü3298 leaves the cluster-completeness question genuinely open.
next_steps: Perform a targeted BLASTP of every canonical Tu3298 epi protein (including epiY) against the KSE56 complete chromosome (deposited alongside pEpi56) to enumerate any chromosomal paralogs.
Compare pEpi56 gene order and intergenic regions to Tu3298 (X62386) to detect any silent/pseudogenized epiY-equivalent on the plasmid.
If strain access is possible, cure pEpi56 and re-run the MW2 braRS susceptibility assay to test biological self-sufficiency.

open_questions.q: Do host-strain immunity genes (epiEFG for epidermin, nukFEG/nukH for nukacin) always co-occur with the corresponding structural/modification genes on the same replicon, and are there any S. epidermidis genomes carrying orphan immunity loci without a producer cluster (which would suggest cross-immunity or a decommissioned bacteriocin producer)?
open_questions.basis: The replication verified that pEpi56 carries epiE/F/G and pNuk650 carries nukF/E/G/H on the plasmid alongside the structural genes, but did not survey the broader S. epidermidis pangenome for the same immunity loci in the absence of producer genes. If orphan immunity is common, it would materially change the interpretation of host-range and self-protection.
next_steps: Query BV-BRC / RefSeq for all annotated S. epidermidis genomes; run hmmsearch with epiEFG and nukFEGH HMMs.
For each hit, check whether the corresponding structural gene (epiA / nukA) is co-located within 20 kb.
Report the fraction of orphan-immunity carriers and their MLST / clonal complex distribution.

open_questions.q: What is the horizontal mobilization potential of pEpi56 and pNuk650, and could either plasmid transfer to S. aureus under realistic co-colonization conditions (e.g., mixed skin biofilm), thereby weaponizing an S. aureus recipient with lantibiotic production?
open_questions.basis: The paper reports the two plasmids as complete circular molecules but does not experimentally test conjugative / mobilizable transfer to S. aureus. Neither the replication nor the paper enumerates rep, mob, oriT, or T4SS-like features. Given the clinical relevance of S. aureus and the fact that MW2 was the indicator, this is a first-order open question.
next_steps: Run oriTfinder / MOBscan / MOB-suite on OK031036 and OK031035 to classify Rep family and detect any relaxase / oriT signatures.
Search the deposited plasmids for T4SS components (virB-like) and IS elements flanking the bacteriocin cluster.
Design a lab-realistic filter-mating assay between KSE56/KSE650 donor and a marked S. aureus recipient (e.g., RN4220) to measure transfer frequency; independent group work.

open_questions.q: How does the biosynthetic diversity of bacteriocin plasmids in S. epidermidis compare to that in other coagulase-negative staphylococci (CoNS) such as S. hominis, S. capitis, S. warneri, and S. lugdunensis --- do they carry orthologs of the pEpi56 / pNuk650 clusters, or are there entirely distinct lantibiotic / sactibiotic families dominating the CoNS plasmidome?
open_questions.basis: The replication scope was restricted to S. epidermidis and a single comparator (pIVK45 from S. simulans-adjacent lineage). The paper's oral-cavity screen touched only S. epidermidis. Broader CoNS comparative genomics is required to know whether the epidermin/nukacin plasmid architecture is species-specific or a shared CoNS phenomenon.
next_steps: Assemble a comparative-plasmidome dataset: all complete CoNS plasmids in RefSeq (est. 500-1500 sequences).
Run BAGEL4 / antiSMASH bacteriocin scans on the plasmid set; cluster hits by RiPP class.
Report cross-species prevalence of epi-like and nuk-like clusters, and identify any novel CoNS-specific lantibiotic families.

open_questions.q: Does the in-silico predicted antibacterial spectrum inferred from pEpi56 / pNuk650 gene content (epidermin + nukacin structural + modification + export machinery all present, immunity loci intact) actually match the wet-lab activity spectrum reported in the paper against 15+ oral/skin commensals --- or are there indicator strains where the in-silico prediction and the observed activity diverge, pointing to receptor-side determinants (e.g., lipid II variant availability, undecaprenyl-P-P-N-acetylmuramoyl-pentapeptide access) that gene calling alone cannot capture?
open_questions.basis: The replication explicitly could not test the paper's wet-lab spectrum claims; only sequence-and-structure claims were replicable in-silico. There is no public benchmark linking predicted bacteriocin gene calls to measured cross-species inhibition, so the wet-vs-in-silico gap is quantitatively unknown.
next_steps: Cross-tabulate the paper's Table of activity vs indicator strains against the presence/absence of lipid II biosynthesis variants and known lantibiotic receptor determinants in those indicators.
For any wet-lab hits or misses that violate the expected pattern, sequence the indicator strains and search for receptor variants.
Prospectively test the pEpi56/pNuk650 gene-content prediction on a panel of never-before-tested CoNS indicators and score prediction accuracy.
